audit.why: Pop Blossom is a 600-range leap that knocks up and then stuns, on 120/105/90s, and Riot's text says the preparation is hidden while Neeko is disguised. That is a lane-relevant spike and a direct answer to Irelia's W charge, which a knockup interrupts.

audit.whatIsWrong: The root was attributed to Blooming Burst (Q) in wants.foe[1] and spikes[0], and to Shapesplitter (W) in spikes[0]. It belongs to Tangle-Barbs (E). Neeko's clone was also credited with a stun it does not have.
audit.why: Riot's text: Blooming Burst is a seed that blooms again, Shapesplitter sends a clone and grants move speed, and Tangle-Barbs is the root — 1000 range, 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s, and it becomes larger, faster and longer-rooting after passing through a champion. The unstated interaction that matters most: Neeko's passive disguise breaks on receiving immobilising crowd control, so Irelia's E strips it.
audit.corrected: Real names throughout; disguise-break written into dosFull[1] and breakdown.carry.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Tangle-Barbs upgrade-on-pass was never mentioned.
audit.why: A root that has already crossed a champion is bigger, faster and lasts longer — so standing behind a teammate is what turns a dodgeable skillshot into a full combo.

edits.before: From levels 3-5 you continue to win skirmishes because your Q-W-E combo out-trades her poke-and-root game plan, especially if you dodge her initial root attempt. Level 6 gives her a strong teamfight ultimate with root and clone burst, but it doesn't flip the underlying 1v1 duel since you can close the gap and kill her before she lands the full combo. You should keep applying pressure whenever she's forced to reveal herself.
edits.after: From levels 3-5 you win skirmishes because your Q-W-E combo out-trades her poke-and-root plan, especially once you dodge the first Tangle-Barbs. Level 6 gives her Pop Blossom — a leap that knocks up and then stuns at 600 range, with the wind-up hidden while she is disguised — so don't W-charge into it and don't facecheck a bush she could be sitting in as a minion. Keep pressuring her whenever she reveals herself.

edits.before: Neeko becomes a strong teamfight threat with pick potential off her ultimate, but she still has no personal escape tool besides Flash, meaning a fed Irelia with Trinity Force can isolate and kill her in skirmishes before her team reacts. Her scaling is about setting up kills for her team, not surviving 1v1s, so as long as you avoid her full combo in the open you remain favored.
edits.after: Neeko becomes a strong teamfight threat with pick potential off Pop Blossom, but her only outs are Shapesplitter's clone and speed boost rather than any dash, so a fed Irelia can isolate her and kill her before her team reacts. Her scaling is about setting up kills for her team, not surviving 1v1s, so as long as you make her spend Tangle-Barbs first you stay favoured.

notes: The suspectNames hit is a real error, not a false positive: wants.foe[1] said 'Land Blooming Burst root' and credited the Shapesplitter clone with a stun. The root is Tangle-Barbs (E) and the stun is Pop Blossom (R); both fixed. Same inherited build contradiction as the other Irelia matchups — content spikes[2] and spikes[3] are written around Trinity Force while report[8] prescribes Blade of the Ruined King into Wit's End. I left spikes[2] and spikes[3] alone because I cannot tell which build the page intends. Not verified from the kits and therefore not asserted: whether Irelia's E grounding stops the Pop Blossom leap, whether the Pop Blossom knockup can be cleansed or reduced by tenacity, and whether Irelia's Bladesurge can target a Shapesplitter clone.
